key_geographic_observations: The real map shows a dense suburban residential grid typical of the Dallas–Plano TX metro area (lat ~33.010–33.037, lon ~-96.720 to -96.688), with regular block-size residential streets covering most of the coverage area.

A major N-S arterial road/corridor runs along the western edge of the map (visible as a wider, highlighted road around lon -96.718 to -96.715), with associated commercial strip development — consistent with higher user density on the western fringe.

The NE corner of the map shows a significant green/park area (visible light-colored open space around lat 33.034–33.037, lon -96.695 to -96.688), which aligns with lower signal contention in that quadrant.

USID_00's tower at (33.023, -96.703) sits within a dense residential grid, explaining the compact, uniformly strong RSRP pattern within its dominance area — no terrain obstructions, flat suburban terrain.
The dominance map (tile_1_1) confirms USID_00's territory is surrounded by USID_27 (NW), USID_29 (E/SE), USID_41 (S), and USID_37 (SE), matching the real-map street grid clustering around the tower.

impact_zones.location: Center — main USID_00 dominance footprint, approximately lat 33.022–33.026, lon -96.706 to -96.700

evidence.signal_evidence: RSRP p50 = -57.0 dBm, 100% of dominant pixels above Excellent threshold (-80 dBm); all blue in RSRP image within yellow boundary.
evidence.sinr_evidence: dominant_area_impact_regime = mostly_mild; target_dom_low_sinr_fraction = 0.6923 (69.2% of dominant pixels have low SINR < 5 dB, i.e., interference-limited); target_dom_sinr_mean = 3.7 dB. Backups already competitive in this regime.
evidence.geographic_evidence: Dense residential grid streets visible in real map around USID_00 tower at (33.023, -96.703); flat suburban layout with no signal-blocking terrain features.
evidence.load_evidence: USID_27 absorbs 61.5% at post_outage_load_factor=0.013 (low); all backup overload_risk=low — no congestion impact for this zone.

impact_zones.location: North — lat 33.025–33.027 boundary, where USID_00 meets USID_27 dominance

evidence.signal_evidence: USID_27 RSRP in USID_00 overlap zone: p50_in_zone = -57.6 dBm, 100% above Good threshold; Excellent (blue) signal visible in northern USID_00 area in USID_27 RSRP image.
evidence.sinr_evidence: sinr_regime_impact_note = mixed (hard_gap_fraction = 0.0625, easy_gap_fraction = 0.5625); moderate SINR transition in roughly one-third of this zone.
evidence.geographic_evidence: Northern portion of residential grid; USID_27 orange dominance visible immediately adjacent in dominance_map_tile_1_1, confirming clean handover boundary at this latitude.

impact_zones.location: East — lat 33.022–33.025, lon -96.701 to -96.699, where USID_00 meets USID_29

evidence.signal_evidence: USID_29 in-zone p50 = -58.83 dBm; RSRP image shows USID_00 area (red dashed) is covered with blue/teal from the E side by USID_29.
evidence.sinr_evidence: sinr_regime_impact_note = mostly_mild (easy_gap_fraction = 0.6364); predominantly interference-limited regime means post-outage signal quality change is minimal.
evidence.geographic_evidence: USID_29 (cyan/teal) visible immediately to the E in dominance_map_tile_1_1 with a clean boundary; residential grid continues eastward with no land-use change.

impact_zones.location: South — lat 33.020–33.022, lon -96.706 to -96.702, southern boundary of USID_00 dominance where no backup is identified

evidence.signal_evidence: Coverage hole fraction = 0.1154 (11.54%, 3 pixels unabsorbed); these pixels have no backup with sufficient signal overlap. From RSRP images, this southern fringe of USID_00's territory is the area where USID_41 (S/SW) and USID_37 (SE) have not fully penetrated northward, and USID_31 (far S) stops well short.
evidence.sinr_evidence: SINR map shows predominantly blue/low values in this area (SINR ~2-5 dB, moderate regime); mixed regime applies given the fringe position.
evidence.geographic_evidence: Real map shows continuous residential grid in this southern fringe zone (lat ~33.021, lon ~-96.703–96.705). No natural or infrastructural break at this boundary. The area between USID_41's yellow boundary (visible S) and USID_00's yellow boundary is occupied by normal suburban streets with no geographic explanation for the gap.
evidence.load_evidence: No backup absorbs these 3 hole pixels — service will be fully lost for users in this sub-zone during USID_00 shutdown.

impact_zones.location: West — near lon -96.716 to -96.718, major N-S road corridor visible on W side of real map

evidence.signal_evidence: This corridor is at the western periphery of USID_00's backup coverage extent (backup pixels, not dominant). RSRP image shows greener (~-70 dBm) values at this distance from the tower.
evidence.sinr_evidence: Area-level sinr_mean = 2.8 dB across the full grid; this western corridor is outside USID_00's dominance so USID_00's shutdown has minimal direct impact here.
evidence.geographic_evidence: Major N-S arterial visible in real map along the western edge (lon ~-96.716) — likely a main boulevard with higher vehicle/pedestrian traffic and commercial activity. This area is not within USID_00's dominance zone so is primarily served by USID_04/USID_14/USID_32 type sites.
evidence.load_evidence: Not a dominant pixel of USID_00; impact is negligible — users here primarily served by other sites.

coverage_hole_geographic_assessment.hole_location_description: Southern fringe of USID_00's dominance area, approximately lat 33.020–33.022, lon -96.706 to -96.703 — the transitional zone between USID_00's southern boundary and the northern reach of backup cells USID_41 and USID_37. Three pixels (11.54% of 26 dominant pixels) are unabsorbed.
coverage_hole_geographic_assessment.land_use_in_hole_area: Dense suburban residential grid streets; no open land, parks, or non-residential use visible in this specific sub-zone of the real map.

load_geographic_context.primary_backup_area_character: USID_27 (primary backup, micro tower at lat 33.025, lon -96.705) is located within the same dense residential grid as USID_00, approximately 200m to the NW. Its micro form factor and proximity to USID_00 explain the high overlap (61.5%). The micro tower is likely a hotspot/capacity booster in a high-density residential block, well-matched to absorbing residential indoor/outdoor users displaced from USID_00.
load_geographic_context.notes: All five backup USIDs (USID_27, USID_29, USID_41, USID_37, USID_31) are within the same suburban residential grid environment. The geographic uniformity (flat terrain, dense street grid, no natural barriers) means there are no significant geographic risk amplifiers — no elevation changes, no bodies of water, no highway-bridge-tunnel gaps that would worsen the coverage hole impact beyond what the signal statistics indicate.

key_findings_for_stage4: USID_00's dominance area and all backup zones lie within a flat, dense suburban residential grid (Plano-area TX suburbs), with no critical infrastructure (hospitals, emergency services, transit hubs) identifiable in the dominance footprint from the real map.

Coverage holes (11.54%) are geographically concentrated in the southern fringe of the dominance area — a residential sub-zone where the gap between USID_41/USID_37 reach and USID_00's southern boundary creates a ~3-pixel service void.

The primary backup USID_27 is a co-located micro site in the same residential block as USID_00, ensuring that the majority of displaced users (61.5%) experience a geographically seamless transition to an adjacent cell.
No real-map geographic feature (terrain, water, highway cut) amplifies the coverage hole risk — the southern fringe gap is purely a radio-geometry artifact, not a geographic isolation problem.
The major N-S arterial on the western map edge lies outside USID_00's dominance area and is not impacted by this shutdown.

reasons: Real map available and used, reducing uncertainty from 'high' to 'medium'.
Land use classification (residential vs. commercial) is based on visual interpretation of the real map — no authoritative land-use dataset was used; minor misclassification possible.
Critical infrastructure presence (hospitals, schools, emergency centers) cannot be conclusively ruled out from map visual alone; no POI data layer was available to confirm.
Coverage hole geographic location is inferred from backup absorption patterns, not directly rendered on a pixel-level spatial map.
